This slice alone: **45/45 judged · 40 PASS / 2 PARTIAL / 3 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED / 0 NOT-RUN**. All 3 FAILs are canonical withheld security rows from probes beside items whose clauses all passed (seat-ruled; none new since 18.4.0). **No clause failed, no regression versus round 1 or 18.4.0.** The 24 `priority:P0` items are their own record (`record-R2-P0.md`).

## Environment fingerprint

- framework objectstack-ai/objectstack **b914e7247f69** (`chore: version packages (#33097)`, the v18.5.0 release sha, 26 first-parent commits past round 1's a557fa38); `ui/` in the same tree; Console built (`pnpm console:build`, 12:42–13:00Z) though no item in this slice needs it.
- **Versions read:** `GET /api/v1/health` → `version: "18.5.0"`; discovery `GET /api/v1/discovery` → `version: "18.5.0"`; `objectstack --version` → `@objectstack/cli/18.5.0 linux-x64 node-v22.23.4`.
- Wave: qa#3 seat #33014, anchor #33761, round 2 (`ROUND2.md`). Round 1 of this slice: #33829.
- Build: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` + `OS_SKIP_DTS=1 turbo build` of the showcase / CLI / dogfood closures (70 packages, 1 m 20 s, 0 cached) + spec rebuilt with dts. Node 22.23.4, pnpm 10.31.0, 4 CPUs, 15 GiB memory cgroup.
- App: stock showcase via `OS_PORT=P objectstack dev --seed-admin -p P -d file:/tmp/qa2/GROUP/db/ITEM.db --no-compile --no-watch`, ports 41150–41173 split per group, one server per runner at a time; scratch app copies (WS layout) for every CLI write, package install, self-pinging connector / external-datasource boot and own-compile boot. The tree's showcase dist and `.objectstack/installed-packages/` were never written (checked; `git status` clean).
- Seed: `--seed-admin` + showcase personas; runtime personas via `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user`, keys / positions / sets via HTTP doors.
- Execution: **parallel**, 4 runner subagents for this slice (opus, effort `high`, ≤3 at a time with the two P0 groups): R2L1 / R2L2 (22 pinned items), R2M1 / R2M2 (23 unpinned items, all driven live).
- Round 1's open product cards in this slice: none had a fix land in a557fa38..b914e724 (#33839–#33842 all open). #33839 (connector descriptor saved active, no inert audit) was re-checked as a probe and **still reproduces**.
- Environment incidents: the memory cgroup OOM-killed one runtime pin batch (R2L1) and one dogfood file (R2L2); each re-run green.

## Scope

`node scripts/checklist-select.mjs touched:a557fa386bc3 --json` at b914e724 → 80 runnable items (2 blocked hidden; 715 files changed), of which this slice is the 45 api / cli / build items minus P0. Every revision below is the one the resolver reported and matched the area JSON (none moved since round 1). No `planned` item.

Method: Tier 1 (22 pinned) re-ran every pin per package (`--maxWorkers=1`, dogfood one file per invocation): R2L1 47 unit files / 1,769 tests + 10 dogfood / 136; R2L2 42 files / 986 tests (incl. 3 dogfood); **0 failed**. Live legs re-driven at b914e724, scored at the layer the pin reaches (RUNNER rule 6). Tier 2/3 (23 unpinned) driven live, every clause. Where `a557fa386..HEAD` touched an item's sources (#33646 flow doors judge served holders, #33621 extension record-mode amounts, #33613 import lookups, #33769 NOT NULL relax on upgrade, #33779 messaging org, #33725 MCP elicitation) the runners drove those paths specifically (details per item in the clause files). ## Parked-on #33761 (checklist accuracy, fixture gaps)

- `api-backend.automation-namespace-address` knownGaps[0] is stale: a second flow holder now installs (`os package install` of a scratch package holding flow `showcase_batch_reminders` was admitted; the flow rule moved from deployment-wide one-holder to the namespace rule, #31696). neg[3]'s rationale ("neither address is served") is stale too: `showcase/…` and `qa_c/…` each serve their own flow (200); only the bare name, `_env` and a third namespace answer 409 naming both holders. neg[3] still scores pass. The #33646 disabled-holder cases cannot be staged over HTTP (installed packages refuse disable/delete 422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED; a writable twin gets 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE) and rest on the runtime unit pins (flow-caller-package 32/0, automation-run-doors-per-slot 77/0, automation-addressed-route 51/0).
- `cli.dev-automigrate-policy` acc[3]: the schemaMode pairing still cannot be staged in the fixture; scored from source `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts:1445/1454`, as in round 1.
- `records-forms.field-unique-enforcement`: the unique-violation envelope now also carries `object`; clause wording still holds. #33779 added a cross-org preference leg to `notification-organization-follows-event.integration.test.ts` (10 → 14 tests) that needs two organizations — same fixture gap.
- `integration-system.connector-degraded-recovery` acc[3]: no early retry at kernel-ready again (5/10/20/40 s) — reword to "may" (timing-dependent). Repeats round 1.
- `integration-system.connector-spec-path-no-escape` step 1: on an `os dev` / `os build` boot the compile-time bundler (`bundle-connector-spec-files.ts`) refuses a bad ref first in its own wording; the runtime loader texts the clauses quote appear only when the artifact still carries a path string. The step should name which layer answers. Repeats round 1.
- `cli.doctor-deprecation-scan`: the .ts-only boundary also excludes `.tsx` while `.spec.ts` / `.d.ts` (comments included) are scanned — worth naming; not-found text "Command codemod not found." (capital C); the fixture used an `os init -t app` scaffold (create-objectstack needs network); only src/ is scanned.
- `records-forms.named-import-mapping` acc[1]: re-import is idempotent only when `writeMode` is unset; an explicit `writeMode:"insert"` overrides the mapping's upsert by design (`import-prepare.ts:588-591`).
- `cli.migrate-meta-codemod`: the semantic migration registry has 607 entries (605 at a557fa38); the advisory block now reads "530 manual change(s)".
- `cli.qa-suite-execution`: the "empty target" probe now passes because the Console is built in this environment. Runner trap: `pnpm --dir APP exec objectstack test 'qa/*.test.json'` resolves the glob inside APP; use the binary's full path.
- `approvals.sla-escalation`: the escalation sweep runs every 5 min with no env knob; runners used a wall-clock offset shim plus the boot catch-up sweep (two real 5-minute ticks observed).
- Runner trap for RUNNER.md: `os dev` silently moves to the next free port when `-p` is taken; confirm the port is free (lsof — the container has no `ss`) before each boot.

## Off-clause probes (RUNNER rule 8)

About 2 h of probe time summed over the four runners (≈ 2–6 min per item), same boots and personas as the clauses (admin, baseline member, contributor / position members, 2FA challenge-only client, osk_ keys, anonymous). Boundary classes: empty / missing / unknown ids and names on every door, blank and repeated parameters, scalar and null bodies, qualified flow addresses (`showcase/…`, `_env/…`, unknown namespace, package id as namespace), uppercase / trailing-space names, opposite postures. Found: the three withheld rows above, and two low product cards — card-R2-API-1 (an object extension whose record-mode amount names a one-segment `currencyField` the served object does not declare saves 200, then every write of that amount is refused naming a non-existent field; the gap is beside #33621's served-object check) and card-R2-API-2 (a manual record share to a user id that does not exist answers 201 and persists an inert `sys_record_share` row; pre-existing). Re-checked: #33839 still reproduces. Observations below the filing bar (not filed): `GET /meta/view?package=` (blank) → 200 unfiltered while the same door refuses a blank `?member=` with 400; the connection door of a disabled oauth instance judges the declaration, not the instance; `If-Match: *` is read as a literal version token; `ensure-customization` judges the `.custom` suffix before package existence; rows created by `/import` get UUID ids while REST creates get short ids; a `migrate meta --write` whose only change cannot be traced prints an empty "Wrote 0 of 1" block; protocol range `^-1` still admitted with a warning; bare `…/runs` 405 sends `allow: GET` while the addressed one sends `allow: GET, HEAD` (open #33026).
